subject: DST gap — demo coverage and rotation plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jon Smith <jon.smith@atlasbank.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: DST gap — demo coverage and rotation plan

Hi team + Jon,

Heads up — US daylight savings (Mar 8) happens three weeks before EU DST (Mar 29) this year, so we get a 3-week window where US and EU local times shift out of sync. That has tripped up a few demo bookings in the past (participants see different wall-clock times and some APAC folks get pushed into odd hours).

AtlasBank has been asking for a steady tri-region demo cadence through March while they evaluate Redwood — we should proactively avoid no-shows and confusion. Proposed approach (attached):
- Offer two confirmed weekly slots for March: one US-friendly (08:30–10:00 PT / 11:30–13:00 ET) and one EU/APAC bridge slot (13:00–14:30 UTC) that maps to late afternoon Europe and evening APAC.
- For the 3-week US/EU mismatch window (Mar 8–28), run a rotation where APAC shifts are covered by a dedicated presenter on rotation. Vanessa — can you own APAC-cover weeks?
- Update calendar invites to include explicit local times for US/EU/APAC and add a note: “Check your calendar timezone — DST change on Mar 8 (US) and Mar 29 (EU).”
- Use the attached CSV for publishing available slots and push updated invites from the shared calendar (link below).

Jon — does that split (one US slot + one bridge slot) work for AtlasBank given London + NYC participants? If you prefer a different anchor time, tell us and we’ll pivot.

Next steps:
1) Volunteers to cover APAC rotation for Mar 8–28.
2) Agree on final times and I’ll push invites and update HubSpot.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: dst-demo-rotation-2026.csv (proposed slots), updated-invite-template.ics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-02-25T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: DST gap — demo coverage and rotation plan

Thanks Soojin — +1 on the two-slot model. A few practical items from scheduling ops: 
- Add an 08:00 UTC / 20:00 JST alternate on Fridays for APAC-heavy bookings (gives APAC teams an early evening option).
- In the invite template, include both UTC and 2 local zones (host + main attendee) so recipients see the mapping.
- Mark the shared calendar events as "Redwood Demo — Confirmed (DST-checked)" so Ops can filter them.

Vanessa — happy to co-own the rotation schedule if you want me to publish the weekly on-call roster in the CSV.

-Marissa

Date: 2026-02-25T14:02:00+00:00
Subject: Re: DST gap — demo coverage and rotation plan

Thanks all for the heads-up. London team prefers afternoon our time (14:00–16:00 GMT), but we can make the 13:00–14:30 UTC bridge slot work on most days. One ask: could we push the recurring invites to show 14:00 local London time explicitly? A few of our folks still see the wrong time when their calendars auto-convert during the DST switch.

Also: if a presenter needs to swap because of an overnight shift, please cc salesops@finledger.io so our scheduling tool can reconcile changes.

—Jon

All — thanks for the quick replies. Summary and next steps: 
1) Agreed model: one US anchor slot + one bridge slot (13:00–14:30 UTC) for March.
2) Vanessa will own APAC rotation weeks Mar 8–21; Karthik covers Mar 22–28. Marissa will publish the alternate Fri APAC slot (08:00 UTC / 20:00 JST).
3) I’ll update the shared calendar and push new invites showing local times explicitly for London and NY. I’ll also add the DST note you suggested.
4) Karthik — please update HubSpot (ATL-2026-093) once invites are out.

Attached: dst-demo-rotation-2026.csv (finalized weekly roster). I also attached an invite template (updated-invite-template.ics) with explicit UTC + attendee local-time copy for calendar bodies.

Best,
